newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares widen gains, Eurotunnel rises.
newsitem.headline: French shares widen gains, Eurotunnel rises.

text.p: French shares widened their gains at midday on Thursday, bolstered by a firmer dollar and bond prices as well as a technical rally on the first day of the May bourse account, dealers said.
The market had been testing resistance at 2,550 points and broke above that level in the afternoon.
On the political front, rivals Prime Minister Alain Juppe and Socialist leader Lionel Jospin will make speeches today.
* CAC-40 index up 23.84, or 0.94 percent, at 2,557.48 at 1055 GMT

* At least three new polls of voters' intentions in the upcoming May/June French parliamentary election will be published next week, while two polls taken before the snap election was called will be released this week, polling organisation officials said on Thursday.

Louis Harris will publish a poll on Thursday at 1400 GMT of French views on the introduction of a single European currency. The poll was conducted on April 18 and 19, before President Jacques Chirac called the snap election.
Morgan Stanley said the worst-case scenario was the right losing its absolute majority, with a 10 percent probability.
* Eurotunnel, up 2.31 percent at 6.65 francs, said it had reached a debt rescheduling agreement with a steering group of banks and added it aimed for an operating break-even in 1997.
* Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, unchanged at 402 francs, due to announce first quarter results after close.
* Rhone-Poulenc, up 1.10 percent at 184.50, benefits from chairman's announcement on Wednesday 1997 asset sales would be five billion francs rather than three billion.
* Accor, down 1.81 percent at 867 francs, suffers from profit-taking.
* L'Oreal, up 3.51 percent at 1,975 francs, boosted by Wednesday meeting at which company said it expected substantial growth. Morgan Stanley raised its price goal to 2,170 francs from 2,100.
* Publicis, up 8.89 percent at 600 francs, leads the gainers in second-day of quick run to recover from losses started in February which ended a rising trend of more than a year.
